author: katspaugh
body:
> Null means no name,
> cache both hit and empty miss —
> Infura sleeps easy.

## What it solves

Resolves: [WA-2092](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-2092/cache-addresses-with-no-ens-resolution)

When ENS name lookup is enabled as a fallback, addresses without a resolvable ENS name were not cached — only positive results were. Every hook mount for such an address triggered a fresh provider (Infura) lookup, which could be abused by rapid re-mounts or repeated navigations.

## How this PR fixes it

`useAddressResolver` now caches both positive and negative lookup outcomes:

- Cache type changed from `Record<string, Record<string, string>>` to `Record<string, Record<string, string | null>>`, where `null` is the sentinel for "no ENS".
- Cache hit check uses `in` (key presence) rather than truthiness, so a cached negative short-circuits the provider call.
- The write now happens inline after `lookupAddress` resolves (replacing the previous `useEffect` that only wrote on positive results).

## How to test it

1. Enable the `DOMAIN_LOOKUP` chain feature on a chain.
2. Enter an address that has no ENS reverse record (e.g. a fresh EOA) in a field that uses `useAddressResolver` (address book entry, tx recipient, etc.).
3. Re-mount the component (navigate away and back, or re-open a modal) with the same address.
4. Inspect network: only the first mount should hit the RPC provider; subsequent mounts resolve from cache.

Unit test `caches no-ENS results so repeated lookups do not hit the provider` covers this.

## Affected flows

- Address display / resolution wherever `useAddressResolver` is used (address book, tx builder recipients, owner lists, send flow).

## Blast radius

- `useAddressResolver` (module-level in-memory cache, scoped per chainId × address, per session)
- Consumers: every component that displays or resolves an address-to-name, on any chain with `DOMAIN_LOOKUP` enabled
- No API contract change, no persistence change, no feature flag change
- Mobile: not affected (web-only hook)

## Risks / not checked

- Transient RPC errors are currently swallowed by `services/ens/index.ts#lookupAddress` and returned as `undefined`. With this change, a transient failure gets cached as "no ENS" for the remainder of the session. Existing behavior was to retry on every mount — this PR trades that for fewer calls. If error-vs-null distinction matters, a follow-up in the ENS service is needed.
- Cache is in-memory and per-session; a page reload still triggers a fresh lookup. Cross-session abuse (many users, many reloads) is not addressed here and would need server-side caching.
- Did not exercise the address book override path manually (no change in that code path; address-book names still short-circuit ENS resolution upstream of the cache).
- Did not test on mobile (web-only file).

## Visual summary

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph Before
    A1[Hook mount] --> B1{Cache hit?}
    B1 -->|ens string cached| C1[Return cached]
    B1 -->|no entry, or null ENS| D1[Call lookupAddress]
    D1 --> E1{Result?}
    E1 -->|string| F1[Write cache, return]
    E1 -->|undefined| G1[Return undefined, NO cache write]
  end
  subgraph After
    A2[Hook mount] --> B2{Key in cache?}
    B2 -->|yes| C2[Return cached string or undefined]
    B2 -->|no| D2[Call lookupAddress]
    D2 --> F2[Write cache string or null, return]
  end
```

- [ ] I've tested the branch on mobile 📱 (N/A — web-only)
- [ ] I've documented how it affects the analytics (if at all) 📊 (no analytics impact)
- [x] I've written a unit/e2e test for it (if applicable) 🧑‍💻
- [x] I've listed affected flows and blast radius, and named what I did not verify 🎯

author: sage-senpai
body:
## Summary

Enhances `ProviderRegistry` with real-time RTT tracking and
least-latency routing (#103).

## Problem

All healthy providers were treated as equivalent — requests were
routed in config order regardless of measured performance. A slow or
geographically distant provider received the same share of traffic as
a fast local one, dragging average and tail latency up.

## Approach

Record an exponential moving average of per-provider RTT on every
successful RPC attempt and use those EMAs to order the failover loop.
Before every provider has produced enough samples the registry falls
back to round-robin so new providers aren't starved of the traffic
they need to build up statistics. Failover behaviour is otherwise
untouched: every healthy provider is still attempted on error.

## Changes

- **`core/src/rpc_provider.rs`** — new `ProviderStats` with EMA over
  `AtomicU64` integer arithmetic (no mutex in the hot path).
  α = 2 / (window + 1), default window 20 samples (~9.5% weight on
  the newest sample). The first sample seeds the EMA directly so the
  series starts on the true value instead of ramping up from zero.
  `ProviderState` gains a `stats` field; `ProviderRegistry` gains
  `record_rtt(url, rtt_us)`, `providers_by_latency()`,
  `stats_snapshot()`, and an `AtomicUsize` cursor that drives the
  round-robin warmup path. `MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_EMA = 10` gates the
  switch from warmup to steady-state.
- **`core/src/routing.rs`** (new) — pure algorithms:
  `select_provider_index` (least-EMA with round-robin fallback and
  lowest-index tie-break) and `compute_inverse_rtt_weights` (for a
  future weighted-round-robin path). They take a `ProviderView` slice
  so tests cover every interesting scenario without booting a
  registry.
- **`core/src/simulation.rs`** — `simulate_transaction_with_failover`
  now drives its loop from `providers_by_latency()` and records the
  measured microseconds of each attempt via `record_rtt`. RTT is
  **not** recorded on `NodeTimeout` / `NetworkError` — those reflect
  client or DNS state rather than the provider's own latency and
  would poison the EMA.

## Algorithm

All arithmetic is integer microseconds: α is stored scaled by 10⁶,
the update multiplies then divides back down. No floating-point in
the request hot path.

## Testing

`core/src/rpc_provider.rs` — registry integration tests:

- `ema_converges_toward_true_value` — 100 identical samples; asserts
  EMA within ±50 µs of the true value.
- `ema_first_sample_seeds_exact_value` — the seed path bypasses the
  convex-combination formula.
- `ema_zero_window_is_clamped_safely` — a caller-supplied
  `window = 0` would have divided by zero; the constructor clamps.
- `is_warmed_reflects_sample_count_threshold` — threshold boundary.
- `providers_by_latency_picks_fastest_once_warm` — steady-state path.
- `providers_by_latency_round_robins_before_warmup` — warmup path,
  cursor rotates by one per call.
- `providers_by_latency_excludes_unhealthy_providers` — fast-but-down
  provider is skipped, slow-but-up provider is returned.
- `providers_by_latency_empty_when_all_unhealthy` — tripped pool.
- `record_rtt_for_unknown_url_is_noop` — lookup-miss safety.
- `stats_snapshot_reflects_recorded_samples` — observer endpoint
  verifies counts and EMAs per provider.

`core/src/routing.rs` — pure algorithm tests:

- `empty_pool_returns_none`, `all_unhealthy_returns_none`,
  `select_provider_picks_fastest_healthy`,
  `select_provider_falls_back_to_round_robin_before_warmup`,
  `round_robin_skips_unhealthy`,
  `unhealthy_providers_are_excluded_from_ema_pick`,
  `ties_broken_by_lowest_index`,
  `inverse_rtt_weights_favour_faster_providers`,
  `inverse_rtt_weights_skip_unhealthy`,
  `inverse_rtt_weights_on_empty_healthy_pool_return_empty`,
  `zero_rtt_is_clamped_to_one_in_weight_calc`.

### ⚠️ Build verification gap

I was unable to run `cargo test` / `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`
locally. The development machine has no working C toolchain: the
`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` rustup default is missing `gcc.exe` and
`dlltool.exe` (required by `ring`, `windows-sys`, `getrandom`,
`parking_lot_core`), and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` has no C++ build
tools workload installed. `cargo check` resolves the whole dependency
graph (validating `Cargo.toml`, module wiring, and imports) before
the C-linker step fails — the failure is environmental, identical to
the block on PRs #98 and #104. Please run CI / review with fresh
eyes; no Rust-level error surfaced during the resolve phase.

## Metrics

`ProviderRegistry::stats_snapshot()` returns a `Vec<ProviderStatsSnapshot>`
with `{ name, url, ema_rtt_us, sample_count }` per provider, ready to
feed a Prometheus gauge or expose on `/health`. Wiring that snapshot
into the actual metrics endpoint is a follow-up — I did not introduce
a new metrics dependency since the project does not currently use
the `metrics` crate.

## Notes / follow-ups

- The `MIN_SAMPLES_FOR_EMA` threshold (10) and default EMA window
  (20) are compile-time constants today. Promoting both to config is
  an obvious follow-up once the operational preferences settle.
- `compute_inverse_rtt_weights` is shipped but not yet wired into any
  dispatch path — the current registry uses pure least-EMA with
  round-robin warmup. The weighted-round-robin variant is ready to
  adopt when a use case justifies it.
- `stats_snapshot` → Prometheus gauge wiring.

## Interaction with PRs #98 and #104

All three branches carry the same
`chore(workspace): exclude typed_data_auth…` commit. Whichever lands
first carries the fix; the others rebase the duplicate away cleanly.

Closes #103

## Summary
- CDP debug port and Electron `userData` are now derived from the project root, so two worktrees running `npm start` don't cross-wire — before this, both bound CDP on 9222 (so a Playwright MCP in worktree B could silently drive worktree A's window) and both wrote to `~/Library/Application Support/CreatorsStudio/folders.json` (last write wins, Chromium profile locks could wedge the second instance).
- `.mcp.json` now points at `scripts/playwright-mcp.mjs`, which recomputes the same SHA-1-based port from `process.cwd()` and spawns `@playwright/mcp` against it. Each worktree's port is also written into `.vite/dev-boot.json` for humans who want to open DevTools at `localhost:<port>`.
- `npm run ensure-dev` is a new idempotent helper: it checks the boot marker + CDP, and if the dev server isn't up it spawns `npm start` detached (logs to `.vite/dev.log`) and blocks until a fresh boot marker lands. Lets Claude self-heal when the dev window is down instead of asking the user to start a terminal. Honors a partial-startup race via the existing reload socket so it doesn't double-spawn.
- Packaged / test builds are unchanged: CDP and the `.vite/userData` default are both gated on `!app.isPackaged`; tests still override via `CREATOR_STUDIO_USER_DATA_DIR`.

## Test plan
- [x] Three Electron instances ran concurrently (`creator-studio-2`, `/tmp/cs-wt-a`, `/tmp/cs-wt-b`); each bound a distinct CDP port (9859 / 10069 / 10196) and got its own `.vite/userData/`. Confirmed that `process.cwd()` and `app.getAppPath()` agree on the derived port on macOS (both resolve the `/tmp` → `/private/tmp` symlink).
- [x] `ensure-dev` verified: already up → no-op in ~100 ms; dead → spawns detached, blocks until CDP is live (~2 s with a warm cache); idempotent rerun right after spawn → reports already-up.

author: cs01
body:
## Before
\`f()[expr]\` where \`expr\` contains another call is a latent segfault waiting to happen. Chad's Boehm conservative GC can't see pointers that live only in LLVM registers; if the index-side call triggers allocation, \`f()\`'s returned array may be collected before indexing reads it.

This was the exact root cause of PR #689's emitError segfault (\`getErrors()[getErrors().length - 1]\`). Cost: days of debugging, multiple closed PRs (#662, #681, #682, #690) that all traced back to this class of bug.

## After
New sema pass \`call-result-index-checker.ts\` rejects the pattern at compile time. Users bind the call result to a \`const\` first — the const puts the pointer on the stack where Boehm can scan it.

\`\`\`ts
// Rejected:
const x = getErrors()[getErrors().length - 1];

// Required:
const errors = getErrors();
const x = errors[errors.length - 1];
\`\`\`

## Description
- Scope: just \`f()[expr]\` / \`f.m()[expr]\` where expr subtree contains a call. Doesn't touch \`f().method(g())\`, \`f().field[g()]\`, or other patterns that may also hit issue #688 — those need the deeper codegen fix.
- Severity: ERROR. \`GRANDFATHERED_FILES\` ships EMPTY — probed \`src/chad-native.ts\`, zero existing violations. Rule applies everywhere from day one.
- Positive fixture: \`tests/fixtures/errors/call-result-indexed-with-call.ts\`.

## Why this isn't the full #688 fix
The full fix is a codegen pass that auto-roots every pointer-typed SSA value to a stack slot before any call that could trigger GC. That's ~200-500 LOC of codegen work across expression-dispatch, member.ts, index.ts, and method-calls.ts. Big, risky, and needs its own IR-diff validation.

This PR is a narrow sema rule that eliminates the one specific syntactic pattern that's burned us most. It's complementary to #688 — after #688 lands, this rule becomes redundant but harmless (and can be deleted).

## Lessons from tonight encoded here
See updated commentary in issue #688. Short version: conservative GC + SSA register promotion = any seemingly unrelated codegen change can silently unmask latent pointer-collection bugs elsewhere. Past week's "Stage 0→1 segfaults" were almost entirely this class.

body:
---
  What does this PR do?

  Adds middleware-managed streaming for two hot GraphQL subscriptions: UsersCount and UsersWithAudioCount. Both are now served from in-memory per-meeting state in
  bbb-graphql-middleware, driven by existing akka-apps events on from-akka-apps-redis-channel — they no longer reach Hasura at all.

  This extends the same "streaming subscription" pattern already used for getCursorCoordinatesStream, getUserVoiceStateStream, getChatMessageStream, and getNotificationStream.

  - New file: internal/streaming_server/usersCountStream.go (scalar counter per meeting)
  - New file: internal/streaming_server/usersWithAudioCountStream.go (per-user set, counts voice.joined == true)
  - config/Config.go — adds the two operation names to StreamingSubscriptionsManagedByMiddleware
  - internal/websrv/reader/reader.go — adds the two subscription query patterns to streamingHandleByMiddlewarePatterns
  - internal/streaming_server/reader.go — dispatches subscribe-time snapshot sends
  - internal/websrv/rediscli.go — allow-lists UserJoinedMeetingEvtMsg, UserJoinedVoiceConfToClientEvtMsg, UserLeftVoiceConfToClientEvtMsg and wires each to its handler; extends
  existing UserLeftMeetingEvtMsg handler with two additional dispatches

  Zero changes to akka-apps, the HTML5 client, or any other subsystem. The existing subscriptions on the client continue to work unchanged.

  Closes Issue(s)

  Closes #

  Motivation

  Under burst-join webinar load at ~200 concurrent users on an 8 vCPU / 15 GiB server, Hasura saturates: measured first-response latencies reach 56 seconds for userCurrentSubscription,
   17 seconds each for UsersCount / UsersWithAudioCount, 22 seconds for VideoStreams. Root cause is O(N²) re-evaluation work — every user-state change triggers Hasura re-queries for
  all N connected clients.

  The middleware already handles the same class of problem for four streaming subscriptions by maintaining in-memory per-meeting state fed by akka-apps Redis events. This PR extends
  that pattern to the two hottest scalar aggregate subscriptions as a proof of concept.

  Measured impact (BBB 3.0.25, 8 vCPU / 15 GiB, LiveKit audio, 4 runs on patched middleware):

  At 200 concurrent users, consistent across 4 runs:
  - joined: 185 → 193 mean
  - audio-recv: 114 → 141 mean (+27)
  - cam-subs: 123 → 164 mean (+41)
  - errors: 15 → 7 mean (-55%)
  - UsersCount / UsersWithAudioCount entries in Hasura trace: 500+ each → 0

  At 300 concurrent users: mixed. 1 of 4 runs saw a meaningful jump; 3 of 4 stayed at ~200-user ceiling. Suggests the pattern works per-subscription but more hot subs need to be
  patched to break past 200.

  Full proposal + measurements available on request.

  How to test

  Smoke test (functional):
  1. Build: ./local-build.sh in bbb-graphql-middleware/
  2. Deploy to a BBB server, restart bbb-graphql-middleware service
  3. Join a meeting in a browser, verify the user count and audio-user count display correctly in the user list panel
  4. Have a second user join, verify counts update for both clients within ~100ms
  5. Leave the meeting, verify counts decrement

  Verification that subscriptions are actually bypassed:
  - Run the middleware with the Hasura tracing proxy in front (or check Hasura's query log)
  - Confirm UsersCount and UsersWithAudioCount no longer appear as live queries against Hasura while user_aggregate-shaped responses continue to arrive at the client

# GXT dual-backend rendering (opt-in preview)

> Re-created from https://github.com/emberjs/ember.js/pull/20711 with an updated
> architecture split, first-class package layout, baseline-gated CI, and a
> draft RFC.

## Summary

This PR adds **Glimmer-Next / GXT** (`@lifeart/gxt`) as an opt-in, build-time
alternate rendering backend for `ember-source`, sitting behind
`EMBER_RENDER_BACKEND=gxt` (production bundles) and `GXT_MODE=true` (the Vite
dev loop). The split happens strictly at the `@glimmer/*` + `ember-template-compiler`
boundary — everything above that line is shared `@ember/*` code, everything
below it is backend-specific. Classic Glimmer remains the default with **no
behavior change and no public API change**; GXT is tree-shaken out of the
classic bundle. A draft RFC (`rfcs/text/0000-gxt-dual-backend.md`) accompanies
the implementation and is intended to be promoted to an `emberjs/rfcs` PR.

## Motivation

- **Smaller runtime model for client-only apps.** GXT is closure-based and has
  no VM opcodes, no wire format, and no template JIT — just reactive cells and
  direct DOM adapters. For apps that do not need SSR or Glimmer-VM-only
  addons, this is a meaningful architectural simplification.
- **Upstream the `@lifeart/gxt` compat work into mainstream Ember** so that
  consumers can evaluate a second backend without a fork. The compat layer is
  Ember-owned code; GXT itself stays an external dependency.
- **Dual-backend posture lets the community measure GXT in real apps** without
  asking the Glimmer team to maintain a second runtime or rewriting GXT's
  reactive core onto VM opcodes (which are architecturally incompatible — see
  RFC §Motivation).
- **Zero-cost to classic consumers.** The classic bundle is byte-for-byte
  identical to pre-PR output on targeted modules; nothing is conditionally
  compiled in the hot path.

## What's in this PR

The compat layer is a first-class private package (`@ember/-internals/gxt-backend`); the classic Glimmer path is unchanged. The branch history is squashed into **area commits that read in review order** (compat layer → vendored `@glimmer/*` seams → classic-side hooks → demo app → build/CI/test infrastructure → RFC draft → dependency bump → baseline refresh), followed by focused, individually-gated hardening commits: the consumable `ember-source-gxt` assembly + Tier-1 acceptance, the `@glimmer/component-gxt` identity fallback, the SSR `withRootContext` seam, retirement of the last string/regex template transforms, a dead-file audit, and CI wiring for the bundle-size gate and the gxt unit tests.

### New package — `packages/@ember/-internals/gxt-backend/`

First-class home for the compat layer (moved out of the previous
`packages/demo/compat/` scratch location). Declared as a private package with
a full `exports` map in its `package.json`. Key files:

- `manager.ts` — the heart of the adapter. Ember component / helper /
  modifier managers translated onto GXT's reactive + lifecycle primitives.
  Large, but organized by internal headers (best reviewed section by section).
- `compile.ts` — template compiler bridge: accepts the Ember `.hbs` / `.gts`
  input shape and produces a GXT template factory. Paired with
  `gxt-template-compiler-plugin.mjs` and `gxt-template-factory.ts`. The Ember
  template dialect ({{outlet}}, {{#each-in}}, {{on}} hash args, bare-helper
  mustaches, `-get-dynamic-var`, yielded block-params, …) is expressed as
  `@glimmer/syntax` AST visitors passed through glimmer-next's
  `CompileOptions.transforms` hook (contributed upstream for this work) rather
  than string rewriting — the dialect source-rewrite path is now **100%
  AST-transform-based** (the final three string scanners — triple-mustache,
  implicit-tbody, HTML-comment preservation — were migrated to visitors and
  deleted; only a structural `{{#in-element insertBefore=}}` keyword-arg
  extraction remains). Post-codegen output patching was removed entirely in
  favor of upstream serializer fixes shipped in `@lifeart/gxt@0.0.64`.
- `reference.ts`, `validator.ts`, `destroyable.ts` — seam shims for
  `@glimmer/reference`, `@glimmer/validator`, `@glimmer/destroyable`.
- `glimmer-tracking.ts`, `glimmer-application.ts`, `glimmer-util.ts`,
  `glimmer-env.ts`, `glimmer-syntax.ts` — drop-in substitutes for the
  corresponding `@glimmer/*` packages.
- `ember-template-compiler.ts`, `runtime-hbs.ts`, `gxt-with-runtime-hbs.ts`,
  `test-compile.ts` — template-compiler entry points across production and
  test harnesses.
- `outlet.gts`, `link-to.gts`, `ember-routing.ts` — router integration.
- `helper-manager.ts`, `ember-gxt-wrappers.ts` — helper manager adapter and
  Ember-side wrappers for GXT primitives.
- `debug.ts`, `debug-render-tree.ts` — debug/render-tree surface (full
  Ember Inspector parity is follow-up work — see RFC §8).
- `__tests__/` — direct unit tests for the adapter, including a
  rehydration-delegate suite.

### Vendored `@glimmer/*` seams and test-harness adaptations

`packages/@glimmer/manager/index.ts` gained no-op stubs for the GXT hook
symbols (`onTag`, `onComponent`, `onModifier`) plus namespace-import-friendly
re-exports so that `tracked.ts` and `internal.ts` resolve identically on both
backends without conditional compilation. On classic, the stubs are
unreachable and stripped by tree-shaking. The group also carries small
interface/type accommodations under `packages/@glimmer/…` and the
`@glimmer-workspace/integration-tests` harness adaptations — including the GXT
rehydration delegate
(`packages/@glimmer-workspace/integration-tests/lib/modes/rehydration/gxt-delegate.ts`).

### Classic-side integration hooks

Edits under `packages/@ember/-internals/glimmer/`,
`packages/@ember/-internals/metal/`, `packages/@ember/object/`,
`packages/@ember/routing/`, and `packages/@ember/runloop/` add the narrow set
of hooks GXT needs to observe and participate (CP re-render cascades,
notifyPropertyChange gating, outlet re-render instrumentation, runloop
scheduling boundaries). **Every change is a no-op on the classic build path**;
they exist only so GXT has something to bind to.

### Demo app — `packages/demo/`

Vite-based demo that exercises the GXT backend end-to-end (`vite.config.mts`,
`src/`, `tests.html`). This is the fastest way to poke at the backend in a
browser and is also what the test runner drives under the hood.

### Build-time aliasing

- `rollup.config.mjs` gained an `EMBER_RENDER_BACKEND=gxt` branch that swaps
  `@glimmer/*` and `ember-template-compiler` aliases for the `gxt-backend`
  entry points. Default remains `classic`.
- `vite.config.mjs` gained the same aliasing under `GXT_MODE=true`, driving
  the dev loop and the Playwright test runner.

### RFC draft

- `rfcs/text/0000-gxt-dual-backend.md` — SemVer posture, feature support
  matrix, FastBoot/engines disposition, `@glimmer/component` disposition,
  Ember Inspector parity plan, numeric exit criteria for leaving preview.
- `rfcs/text/0000-gxt-dual-backend-addon-matrix.md` — best-effort
  top-20-addon compat snapshot (7 pass / 4 classic-only / 9 untested;
  every "pass" is inference, not yet verification).

### CI

- `.github/workflows/gxt-dual-build.yml` — builds both backends on every PR,
  runs bundle-size check per backend, uploads artifacts.
- `.github/workflows/gxt-smoke.yml` — 4-shard Playwright smoke suite on every
  PR, required check, finishes in under 5 minutes.
- `.github/workflows/gxt-full.yml` — nightly full suite, compares against
  `test-results/gxt-baseline.json`, opens a regression issue on green→red.

### Tooling

- `scripts/gxt-test-runner/` — Playwright + QUnit runner replacing the
  earlier stuck-detection prototype. Runs the whole suite in a **single
  browser tab** (one shared context/page across all ~920 modules, with a
  session recycle every 50 modules to bound renderer GC debt and a one-shot
  retry for cold boot timeouts). `QUnit.on('runEnd', …)` is the **only**
  completion signal; hangs are recorded as timeouts, never baselin

## Summary

Mirror of [HarperFast/harper#402](https://github.com/HarperFast/harper/pull/402)'s latest commit (`fae521c`), which addressed a deep external review. Applying the same finding-fix set to oauth's live workflows.

### Fixed

- **#5 label match tightened** — explicit whitelist (`claude-fix:typo|docs|deps|bug`) instead of `startsWith('claude-fix:')`. Rules out typoed variants.
- **#6 heredoc marker** — random `EOF_$(openssl rand -hex 16)` instead of fixed `CLAUDE_SCOPE_EOF`. Collision-proof against any content a future layer file might include.
- **#7a eager `npm ci` on mention** — dropped. Most mentions don't need deps; prompt tells the agent to install before scripts that do. issue-to-pr keeps its eager install.
- **#8a mention model** — Sonnet 4.6 default with Opus 4.7 opt-in via case-insensitive word-boundary `deep` anywhere in the comment. "Needs deep review" escalates; "fix this typo" stays on Sonnet.
- **#9 scope-to-diff** — review prompt now directs the agent to start from `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` and expand only when a finding demands it.

### Mention-parsing step (new)

Enforces `@claude` as the first non-whitespace token (word-boundary after). Rules out:
- `@claudette` and other substring collisions
- Inline prose references ("I saw @claude's fix")
- Quoted replies (`> @claude …`) where `@claude` is addressing a human

Subsequent steps guard on `steps.mention.outputs.proceed == 'true'` so non-matching comments exit cleanly without running the agent.

### Comment sharpening

- **#1 postinstall RCE** — the allowlist comment previously implied no-arg `Bash(npm install)` was a real mitigation. It blocks `npm install @attacker/x` but not the `postinstall`-via-`Write(package.json)` chain. Comment now names this path. Actual guardrails are branch protection + the author_association gate.
- **#2 `Bash(git:*)` rationale** — review.yml's comment now clarifies "this workflow is READ-ONLY by design" and notes the authoring workflows grant broader git access bounded by branch protection.

### Not applicable to oauth

- **#3 (ai-review-log step)** — oauth already has it.
- **#4 (dead `documentation/**` glob)** — oauth uses the real `docs/` dir.

## Summary

Brain's priority ask after decomper's #208 finding: investigate
the `mwldarm` pool-word quirk that breaks cross-object `.s` tail
calls. Research writeup in the shape of
[`thumb-align-wall.md`](../docs/research/thumb-align-wall.md) —
peer-project survey, bit-pattern analysis, ranked fix paths.

## The observed defect

```asm
; Inside a .s file.
    ldr     ip, =Task_InvokeLocked    ; expected 0x02006870
    bx      ip                         ; pool resolves to 0x40086870
```

At link time `mwldarm` emits the wrong pool word. Executing `bx
ip` branches into unmapped memory on real hardware.

## Bit-pattern analysis

| Bits | Expected | Observed | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[31:24]` | `0x02` | `0x40` | +0x3E |
| `[23:16]` | `0x00` | `0x08` | +0x08 |
| `[15:0]`  | `0x6870` | `0x6870` | 0 |

Low 16 bits correct. Upper half mutated in a non-obvious way —
rules out byte-swap, instruction encoding, and NDS memory-map
veneer.

## Peer-project survey — the useful finding

**No** peer project ships `ldr ip, =sym; bx ip` where `sym` is
cross-object. Every peer keeps pool-word generator + target in
the same TU. Pokediamond / pokeheartgold / pokeplatinum use
`b sym` (PC24 direct branch) for cross-object tail calls in
range, and `ldr pc, =sym` via explicit pool for the minority
case.

## Hypotheses (ranked)

| # | Hypothesis | Likelihood | Testable via |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Pool dedup loses section base | ~70% | Add adjacent constant, observe if pool word shifts |
| H2 | `R_ARM_SBREL32` section-base mis-resolve | ~20% | `objdump -r` on the .o to see reloc type |
| H3 | Interworking veneer intercept | ~8% | Swap `ip` → `r0`, see if value changes |
| H4 | Unresolved-reloc sentinel | ~2% | `mwldarm -v` for warnings |

## Fix paths ranked

- **Path B** (`b sym` direct branch) — same-module tail calls,
  fits Task_* cluster. Zero extra lines.
- **Path C** (explicit `.word sym` pool) — fallback for cross-
  state interworking. One extra line per call-site.
- **Path A** (inline `asm void` in `.c`) — decomper's current
  workaround. Works but loses the `.s`-file pattern brief 013
  established.
- **Path D** (deep mwld investigation) — days of work, only if
  B/C don't suffice.
- **Path E** (mwld flag search) — 30 min exploration, low
  probability of a silver-bullet flag.

**Recommendation**: Path B for same-module cases, Path C for
cross-state. Together they cover essentially every cross-object
tail-call need without toolchain-level changes.

## Suggested next steps

Concrete verification plan for brain + decomper: try Path B on
#208's specific repro, escalate to C if out of range, D/E only
if neither path handles an observed case. Add whichever works
to `decomp-workflow.md` alongside the brief-013 `.s` precedent.

## Test plan

- [x] 872 tests pass unchanged (no code)
- [x] `ruff check` clean (no code)
- [x] Peer-project references verified (URLs + filenames exist)
- [ ] Decomper runs the Path B / C verification on their
      local tree — this doc enables that, doesn't do it

## Scope

`docs/research/mwld-pool-word-wall.md` only. No tool/test/config
changes.

## Pairs with

- `docs/research/thumb-align-wall.md` — the prior mwld/mwcc
  quirk writeup that this doc mirrors in shape
- PR #135 — `.s` file that uses `.word sym` explicitly (Path C
  equivalent) and works — corroborates H1/H2
- PR #165 — cascade-2 wave that renamed Task_InvokeLocked,
  making the cross-object tail-call scenario real
- PR #208 (decomper) — the precipitating finding

Keep `scripts/start-local-dev.sh` attached when it is running inside Codex so the Codex command runner does not clean up the background dev server process tree as soon as the startup script exits.

body:
Share links generated on GitHub Pages dropped the `/planny-planny/` base, producing 404s like `https://colinccook.github.io/invite/<token>` instead of `https://colinccook.github.io/planny-planny/invite/<token>`. The same root cause affected the public share link, the service worker, and the PWA manifest.

### URL helpers
- New `src/lib/appUrl.ts` exposing `buildAppUrl` / `buildInviteUrl` / `buildShareUrl`, all backed by `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`.
- `InviteManager` and `PublicShareToggle` now build copy/display URLs through the helpers.

```ts
// before
const url = `${window.location.origin}/invite/${token}`
// after
const url = buildInviteUrl(token) // → https://colinccook.github.io/planny-planny/invite/<token>
```

### Other base-path bugs found in the same sweep
- `index.html`: SW registration uses `%BASE_URL%sw.js` with a matching `scope` (was hardcoded `/sw.js`, silently failing on Pages).
- `public/sw.js`: `STATIC_ASSETS` switched to paths relative to the SW scope (was absolute `/`, `/index.html`, …).
- `public/manifest.json`: `scope` and `start_url` made relative (`./`) so an installed PWA launches into the app, not the domain root.

### Deploy flexibility
- `vite.config.ts` accepts a `BASE_PATH` env override, so a custom domain (e.g. `plannyplanny.app` at the apex) is a workflow change, not a code change.

```ts
base: process.env.BASE_PATH ?? (process.env.GITHUB_PAGES ? '/planny-planny/' : '/')
```

### Test coverage
- Unit tests for the helpers across dev (`/`), GitHub Pages (`/planny-planny/`), nested subpaths, apex domains, and default-argument behaviour, with explicit regression guards for the broken URL shape from the bug report.
- `InviteManager` / `PublicShareToggle` tests assert the copied (and, for share, displayed) URL contains the base path.
- New BDD feature `tests/features/household/invite-link.feature` exercises the invite route end-to-end (unauth → register redirect with token preserved, app actually renders, route lives under the base). Public-sharing feature gains a base-path routing scenario.

### Lint hardening (per review request)
- ESLint bumped from `tseslint.configs.recommended` → `strict` + `stylistic`.
- Fallout fixed across 14 files: non-null assertions replaced with guards/optional chaining, dynamic `delete` rewritten, empty arrow stubs swapped for `vi.fn()`, `Array<T>` → `T[]`, one `type` → `interface`.
- TypeScript was already at its strictest (`strict` + `noUnusedLocals`/`noUnusedParameters`/`noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`/`noUncheckedSideEffectImports`); no changes needed there.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- ESLint type-checked variants (`strictTypeChecked` / `stylisticTypeChecked`) would add `no-floating-promises`, `no-misused-promises`, etc. — worth a separate pass.

body: ## Summary Fixes the unresolved SSRF bypass bugs identified by Devin Review on PR #1. The `isSafeUrl` function could be bypassed using IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, `::ffff:169.254.169.254`) which passed all existing checks, allowing access to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints. ### Changes 1. **IPv4-mapped IPv6 normalization** — Extract the embedded IPv4 from `::ffff:x.x.x.x` addresses before applying the private-IP regex. Previously `::ffff:127.0.0.1` bypassed all checks. 2. **Check all DNS results** — Use `dns.lookup(hostname, { all: true })` and reject if *any* resolved address is private. The old code only checked the first result, so a hostname resolving to both public and private IPs could slip through. 3. **Block unspecified address (`::`)** — Was not checked before. 4. **Widen IPv6 link-local coverage** — Old regex `/^[fF][eE]80/` only matched `fe80` but RFC 4291 link-local spans `fe80::/10` (`fe80`–`febf`). Now matches `/^[fF][eE][89aAbB]/i`. 5. **Block IPv6 multicast (`ff00::/8`)** — Added `/^[fF]{2}/i` check. 6. **Additional private IPv4 ranges** — Added `100.64.0.0/10` (CGNAT), `198.18.0.0/15` (benchmarking), `240.0.0.0/4` (reserved). ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Verify `::ffff:127.0.0.1` and `::ffff:169.254.169.254` are now blocked (previously bypassed SSRF protection) - [ ] Verify legitimate public URLs (e.g. APKPure, APKCombo) still download successfully - [ ] Confirm the `isPrivateIPv4` regex doesn't false-positive on valid public IPs (e.g. `100.0.0.1` should pass, `100.64.0.1` should block) **Suggested test plan:** Start the server locally, then test the `/api/download-apk` endpoint with URLs resolving to private addresses and confirm 403 responses. Also test with a real APK download URL to confirm normal downloads still work. ### Notes Addresses the unresolved finding from [Devin Review on PR #1](https://github.com/Praashon/APK_Downloader/pull/1#discussion_r3138283548) and also incorporates related feedback from CodeRabbit and Copilot reviews on the same PR. ## Problem

User reported Settings still fails after PR #190. Error was the same UNIQUE violation — after clicking Settings, closing via X, then clicking Settings again, the insert fails.

## Root cause

PR #190 nulled scope_key in \`SessionService.closeSession\`, but client-initiated closes go through a different path:

- The **X close button** in SettingsView → \`onSessionClose\` → \`SessionContext.closeSession\` → \`DELETE /api/sessions/:id\` → \`SessionService.closeSession\` ✓
- But the **DELETE route** might also route through \`updateSession({ status: "closed" })\` in some code paths, and  
- The **client reducer** may dispatch DELETE while the server uses UPDATE for certain transitions

Checking the DB after the user's repro:
\`\`\`
c1ce3465-0c83-4ff3-862c-e2ef66a33cad | Settings | closed | settings
\`\`\`

scope_key was NOT nulled — so the close went through \`updateSession\`, not \`closeSession\`.

## Fix

\`SessionService.updateSession\` now detects \`status → closed | trashed\` transitions and nulls \`scope_key\` in the same UPDATE (unless the caller explicitly sets scope_key). Complements the direct \`closeSession\` and \`worktree-trash-service\` fixes from PR #190.

Also: \`resolveSingletonCarrierProjectId\` now validates the active node's id exists in \`projectTree.projects\` before returning it — guards against stale activeNode state.

- [x] lint 0 warnings

## Summary

Wires the Save handlers that Agent D had to leave disabled in PR #449 because the backing tables didn't exist.

- **Notification Rules page** — now reads/writes `hostel_notification_rules` via batch upsert on dirty rows (amber ring + "Save N changes" counter pattern copied from Agent D's maintenance-sla).
- **General Settings page** — now reads/writes `hostel_general_settings` via single-row upsert on conflict (institution_id). All inputs active, dirty detection gates the Save button.
- Both pages honor the `campus_living.settings.edit` permission + `isSuperAdmin` OR-bypass (PR #395 pattern) and use `useAuth().profile` (never `user`) per PR #407.

## Files

- `lib/services/campus-living/hostel-notification-rules-service.ts` (NEW) — `listRules`, `upsertRules`, `getRuleByEventKey`. Follows `string | undefined` institution_id convention (memory: `feedback_service_institution_id_signature_convention`).
- `lib/services/campus-living/hostel-general-settings-service.ts` (NEW) — `getSettings` (`.maybeSingle()`), `upsertSettings`.
- `hooks/campus-living/use-hostel-notification-rules.ts` (NEW) — React Query wrapper + batch-upsert mutation.
- `hooks/campus-living/use-hostel-general-settings.ts` (NEW) — React Query wrapper + single-row upsert mutation.
- `app/(routes)/campus-living/settings/notification-rules/page.tsx` — replaced display-only grid with a wired matrix (16 events across 5 categories x email/SMS/push).
- `app/(routes)/campus-living/settings/general/page.tsx` — replaced disabled form with a dirty-tracked, validating form (curfew, visitor, mess sections).

## Coordination

**Part of `/myjkkn-chain` Phase 2 — depends on Agent F tables (PR TBD). Coordinator sequences merge.** If this ships before Agent F's migration the Save mutation will toast an error ("relation does not exist"); reads gracefully handle the empty state.

## Design decisions

- **Deferred shared-form extraction.** Each page keeps its own form; no shared `settings-form` component this round. Can be pulled out once all 6 settings pages are wired and patterns have crystallized.
- **Catalog in page file, not DB-driven.** The 16 notification events are declared as a module-level `CATALOG` constant in `notification-rules/page.tsx` with stable `event_key` strings. Keeps UI labels in sync with code and avoids an extra seed-migration round-trip. Agent F's seed should populate default rows matching this catalog; if the DB has rows not in the catalog they're simply not shown (and not lost — still in the DB).
- **Academic-year + semester kept as free-form text/select.** Proper FK to `academic_years` is deferred to a follow-up once Agent F's follow-up migration exposes a selector.
- **`id` intentionally omitted from upsert payload.** We conflict on `(institution_id, event_key)` and `(institution_id)` respectively, not on `id`. Passing a stale id from the client would risk over-writing the wrong row after a re-seed.

## Test plan

- [ ] Agent F's tables land on prod before this merges (coordinator sequencing).
- [ ] Navigate to `/campus-living/settings/notification-rules` as super_admin → toggles render with seeded values, amber ring on modified cells, "Save N changes" counter correct, Save persists.
- [ ] Same page as `campus_living.settings.edit` grantee → same behavior.
- [ ] Same page as read-only role → toggles disabled, read-only banner shown.
- [ ] Navigate to `/campus-living/settings/general` as super_admin → form seeded from DB (or defaults on first load), all fields editable, dirty detection flips Save on.
- [ ] Edit + save + refresh → persisted values round-trip correctly (time fields normalized to HH:MM).

Removed constants no longer referenced anywhere: `BRAND_SECONDARY_DARK`, `CHART_HEIGHT_MOBILE`, `HOVERTEMPLATE_{SALES,APC,COUNT}`, `RADIUS_{SM,MD,LG}`, `SHADOW_{MD,LG}`, `TABLE_ACHIEVEMENT_{GREEN,YELLOW,RED}` (the achievement trio was superseded by `ACHIEVEMENT_*_BG/TEXT` pairs in Phase 2a). `SHADOW_SM` kept — still used by `clipboard_ui`. `BRAND_DARK` / `BRAND_LIGHT` / `SURFACE_RAISED` kept — pinned in the drift test to keep the CSS tokens authoritative.

The old rule at ≤480px did `flex-direction: column` on every `[data-testid="stHorizontalBlock"]`, which flattened icon rows, Yes/No dialogs, and `[1,2,1]` centering layouts into full-width stacks (the audit finding: "make opt-in rather than blanket"). - `stPlotlyChart`, `stDataFrame`, `stMetric`
- `stTextInput`, `stNumberInput`, `stTextArea`, `stSelectbox`, `stDateInput`, `stFileUploader`

Compact rows (icon buttons, spacers, confirm-dialog buttons) stay horizontal. Requires `:has()` — Chrome 105+, Safari 15.4+, Firefox 121+ (~95%+ of users); older browsers get row layout as a harmless fallback. Replaced the two `st.spinner` calls with `st.status` containers that include file count, total MB on parse, and on completion swap to a tick with a concrete summary:
- **Parsing** → "Parsing 3 files (4.2 MB)…" → "Parsed 3 files → 21 days across 2 outlets" ✓

# Feature: Benutzerverwaltung, Typ-basiertes Rollenmodell & Kontoverknüpfungen

## 📖 Beschreibung
Dieses Feature überarbeitet das Benutzer- und Berechtigungsmanagement im Admin-Bereich. Es führt eine strikte Trennung zwischen Kundentypen (Privat/Business) und internen Mitarbeitern (`INTERNAL`) ein, setzt ein Single-Role-Modell (genau eine Rolle pro Nutzer) durch und bietet umfassende Lifecycle-Aktionen (Anlegen, Deaktivieren, Reaktivieren, Soft-Delete). Zudem können administrativ Konten verknüpft werden (z. B. das private Kundenkonto eines Mitarbeiters mit seinem internen Admin-Konto).

---

## 🧑‍💻 User Stories & Akzeptanzkriterien

### US-1: Typ-basiertes Single-Role-Modell
**Als Administrator** möchte ich Benutzern einen klaren Kontotyp (Privat, Unternehmen, Intern) und exakt eine primäre Rolle zuweisen, **damit** die Rechteverwaltung eindeutig bleibt und Kunden strikt von internen Mitarbeitern getrennt sind.

- [ ] **AK 1.1:** Im Dialog zur Rollenbearbeitung und Benutzeranlage kann der `UserType` (Privatkunde, Unternehmen, Intern) über ein Dropdown gewählt werden.
- [ ] **AK 1.2:** Wenn der Typ `Intern` gewählt ist, können interne Rollen (z. B. Admin, Vertrieb, Lager, Mitarbeiter) ausgewählt werden.
- [ ] **AK 1.3:** Wenn der Typ `Privatkunde` oder `Unternehmen` gewählt ist, wird automatisch die Rolle `Kunde` zugewiesen (und interne Rollen sind gesperrt).
- [ ] **AK 1.4:** Es kann *immer nur exakt eine Rolle* pro Benutzer zugewiesen werden (Nutzung von Radiobuttons statt Checkboxen im UI; DB-Constraint `uq_user_roles_single_role`).
- [ ] **AK 1.5:** Lockout-Schutz: Ein Administrator kann sich selbst nicht die Admin-Rolle entziehen.

### US-2: Erweitertes Account-Lifecycle-Management
**Als Administrator** möchte ich Benutzerkonten manuell anlegen, deaktivieren, reaktivieren oder löschen können, **damit** ich volle Kontrolle über die Systemzugänge von Mitarbeitern und Kunden habe.

- [ ] **AK 2.1:** Administratoren können über einen "Benutzer anlegen"-Button neue Konten direkt im System erstellen (inkl. Username, E-Mail, Passwort, Typ und Rolle).
- [ ] **AK 2.2:** Benutzer mit dem Typ `Intern` können *ausschließlich* von Administratoren angelegt werden (Schutz im Backend).
- [ ] **AK 2.3:** Aktive Benutzerkonten können per Knopfdruck deaktiviert werden (Login nicht mehr möglich). Administratoren können ihr eigenes Konto nicht deaktivieren.
- [ ] **AK 2.4:** Deaktivierte Konten können per Knopfdruck wieder reaktiviert werden.
- [ ] **AK 2.5:** Soft-Delete: Ein Konto kann gelöscht werden. Dabei wird es deaktiviert und die Identitätsdaten werden anonymisiert (z. B. `deleted_123` und `deleted_123@deleted.invalid`). Solche Konten können nicht reaktiviert werden.

### US-3: Kontoverknüpfungen (Account Links) verwalten
**Als Administrator** möchte ich verschiedene Benutzerkonten derselben natürlichen Person (z. B. Mitarbeiterkonto und privates Kundenkonto) miteinander verknüpfen, **damit** diese im CRM zusammenhängend betrachtet werden können.

- [ ] **AK 3.1:** In der CRM-Detailansicht gibt es ein Panel "Verbundene Benutzerkonten".
- [ ] **AK 3.2:** Über ein Suchfeld (Autocomplete) können andere aktive Accounts gesucht und mit dem aktuellen Konto verknüpft werden.
- [ ] **AK 3.3:** Ein Benutzerkonto kann nicht mit sich selbst verknüpft werden.
- [ ] **AK 3.4:** Verknüpfte Konten werden tabellarisch/als Liste dargestellt (inkl. Name, E-Mail und aktuellen Rollen-Tags).
- [ ] **AK 3.5:** Bestehende Verknüpfungen können über einen Button "Entfernen" getrennt werden.

### US-4: Optimierte Suche und Filterung im Admin-Dashboard
**Als Administrator** möchte ich die Benutzerliste effizient durchsuchen und filtern können, **damit** ich auch bei vielen Datensätzen schnell den gewünschten Account finde.

- [ ] **AK 4.1:** Die Suchleiste ermöglicht die Suche nach ID, Benutzername, E-Mail oder Kundennummer. (Bei Eingabe einer reinen Zahl wird gezielt nach der ID oder Kundennummer gesucht).
- [ ] **AK 4.2:** Ein Filter nach "Status" (Alle, Aktiv, Inaktiv) ersetzt den bisherigen Switch, um präziser nach deaktivierten Konten zu suchen.
- [ ] **AK 4.3:** Die Tabelle zeigt Status-Badges (z. B. "Aktiv" in Grün, "Inaktiv" in Grau) für einen schnellen visuellen Überblick.
